meta.title: Views of the transformation
meta.question: Was the change of system after 1989 worth it?
meta.measure: Average view of the change of system after 1989, from 0 (not worth it, more losses) to 10 (worth it, more gains)
meta.anchor: Pooled from every question on the change of political and economic system after 1989, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Compared with the communist regime, has the country's economic situation improved, stayed the same or got worse?
Comparing the present political system with the previous one: previous system better, neither, present system better
items.notes: CEEB 3 (1992) only; the label check keeps V285 of other waves out.

items.wording: Did the past four years (1993) / the political changes of 1989-93 (1998) bring more gains or more losses? (only gains ... only losses)
items.notes: POLPAN 1993 and 1998. The 1998 wave asks about the changes of 1989-93 specifically.

items.wording: Looking back, was it worth changing the system in Poland (5/10/12/15/20 years ago, in 1989)? (definitely worth it ... definitely not)
items.notes: CBOS 1994-03 to 2014-02 (16 surveys); the number of years in the wording changes with the anniversary. 1999-10 and 2005-08 label the ends "definitely yes/no".

items.wording: Since 1989, has much changed for the better in Poland, a little for the better, a little for the worse, much for the worse, or has practically nothing changed? (nothing changed = 5)
items.notes: CBOS 1996-09, 1997-05, 1999-04, 2004-05. The companion question about the respondent's own locality is not used.

items.wording: Have the changes in Poland since 1989 brought people more gains or more losses? (only gains ... only losses)
The present political system compared with the system before 1989: much better ... much worse
Have the changes since 1989 brought people more gains than losses, as many of each, or more losses than gains?
The economy now compared with before 1989: much better ... worse
items.notes: PGSW 2000 presidential study (single survey); the PGSW question.

items.wording: How the economy works now compared with before 1989: much better ... much worse
Have the changes after 1989 brought our country more opportunities than threats, more threats than opportunities, or both equally?
Overall, do you approve or disapprove of the political changes that have taken place here since 1989?
Compared with the end of the 1980s, has the state of the Polish economy improved or deteriorated? (definitely improved ... definitely deteriorated; not changed = 5)
items.notes: CBOS 2009-01 and 2014-02; CBOS's counterpart of PGSW's economy-before-1989 question. The other aspects in the battery (security, education, honesty...) are not used.

items.wording: Looking back, were the costs of the transformation after 1989 far too high, high but worth bearing, or not very high (relative to its results)?
Is the economic situation for most people today better, worse, or about the same as it was under communism?
Thinking back to 1989, do you approve or disapprove of the change from a state-controlled economy to a market economy?
Starting in late 1989 we changed from a one-party state to a multiparty system: do you strongly approve, approve, disapprove or strongly disapprove of this change?
items.notes: Pew 2009 fall, 2016, 2019. The East German and former Soviet versions are not matched.

items.wording: How much have ordinary people benefited from the changes since 1989: a great deal, a fair amount, not too much, not at all?
items.notes: Pew 2009 fall and 2019. The parallel questions about business people and politicians are not used.
